newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-ARDILES CELEBRATES AS SHIMIZU BEAT KAWASAKI TO WIN CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARDILES CELEBRATES AS SHIMIZU BEAT KAWASAKI TO WIN CUP.

text.p: Coach Ossie Ardiles, the former Argentinian World Cup winner, was celebrating on Thursday after his side Shimizu S-Pulse won the J.League Nabisco Cup beating cup holders Verdy Kawasaki 5-4 in a penalty shootout after a 3-3 extra-time draw.

Shimizu won after Kawasaki's Brazilian striker Magron missed the second penalty in the shootout before a crowd of 28,232 at Tokyo's Olympic Stadium. Even a hat-trick from the Brazilian striker Bismarck was not enough to bring Kawasaki victory.
Ardiles, a member of the Argentina team which won the World Cup in 1978 and who played for the bulk of his career for Tottenham in England, took over as coach of Shimizu earlier this year.
He said afterwards: "I was nervous throughout the match, in which we gave all we had."

Shimizu are currently placing 12th in the 16-team J.League table. Kawasaki failed to retain the title following its victories in the previous three J.League Cups in 1992-1994. The league cup was not held last year.

Following a lackluster first half, Shimizu's striker Kenta Hasegawa opened the scoring after 68 minutes and Shimizu seemed to have the game wrapped up when Argentine midfielder Oliva headed home to make it 2-0 with nine minutes to go.
But in the closing minutes, Bismarck scored twice to take the game into extra time.
Shimizu regained the lead within a minute of the extra period when midfielder Santos stabbed home a volley from a low cross from Hideki Nagai before Bismarck equalised again 15 minutes later.
